exploratory_logged_plan.E1: the main claim's statistics (pooled, per family, mean of the within-family values, ranked within family) with x = random search's false acceptance at budget 1
exploratory_logged_plan.E2: Spearman with x at 1,000 minus Spearman with x at budget 1, on the pairs holding both, the same clusters resampled jointly

wording.above: the search adds predictive value beyond a check on logged plans
wording.includes: the prediction does not need the search: one logged plan per instance, judged by the emulator and the engine, predicts as well, so the audit cannot be told from a calibration check on logged plans
wording.below: one logged plan predicts better than the search audit

exploratory_logged_plan.wording_rows: c120 (both RL variables); the 40- and 80-city rows are reported beside them

decision_79.main: results.main_d79: within-family permutation null of the pooled Spearman (2000 permutations, seed 0); sensitivities (clustered by task family; leave one lineage out; Pearson); the within-family reading; its power by simulation

main_wording.null_above: exceeds what the differences between task families alone produce
main_wording.null_not_above: is no more than the differences between task families produce
main_wording.within_excludes: within a task family the audit ranks emulators
main_wording.within_includes: does not rank emulators within a task family

decision_79.main_power_assumptions: In each task family, the checkpoints' (audit, RL) values are bivariate normal with the stated true Spearman (Pearson 2 sin(pi rho / 6)); families and checkpoints independent (no checkpoint effect shared across families, which the measured intra-checkpoint correlations, near zero and negative, do not contradict); continuous values (no ties); the row's numbers of checkpoints and families; the statistic and interval as computed here (mean of the within-family Spearman, cluster bootstrap over checkpoints, percentile), with 1000 resamples in place of 2,000; 500 simulations per cell; power = the share whose 95 per cent interval excludes zero.
decision_79.secondary: results.secondary_d79: the analysis plan's verdict on the checkpoint set (24 if every half-trained checkpoint has test_half/ fidelity, else the 12 finals), checkpoint-level rows, power to falsify at a true |Spearman| of 0.5 by simulation

secondary_wording.not_falsifiable: not falsified, and not falsifiable at this size

decision_79.secondary_power_assumptions: A true Spearman of 0.5 (either sign) between the fidelity measure and the checkpoint's mean false acceptance over the five families; the measure constant across a checkpoint's families; a pair's false acceptance = the observed grand mean + the observed family effect + (the observed SD of checkpoint means) x the checkpoint component + a normal residual of the observed residual SD (two-way additive fit on the row's own checkpoints), centred within the checkpoint; normal, continuous values (the observed rates are discrete); the row's checkpoints; the statistics and intervals as computed here, 1000 resamples in place of 2,000; 500 simulations; power = the share whose interval on |Spearman| lies above 0.3 (the analysis plan's rule).

secondary_d79.power_assumptions: A true Spearman of 0.5 (either sign) between the fidelity measure and the checkpoint's mean false acceptance over the five families; the measure constant across a checkpoint's families; a pair's false acceptance = the observed grand mean + the observed family effect + (the observed SD of checkpoint means) x the checkpoint component + a normal residual of the observed residual SD (two-way additive fit on the row's own checkpoints), centred within the checkpoint; normal, continuous values (the observed rates are discrete); the row's checkpoints; the statistics and intervals as computed here, 1000 resamples in place of 2,000; 500 simulations; power = the share whose interval on |Spearman| lies above 0.3 (the analysis plan's rule).
